query: Casting is the predominant fabrication method for high-entropy alloys, but solidification-related porosity and microstructural nonuniformity can cause heterogeneous properties. Studies of other high-entropy-alloy compositions have reported high hardness and notable compressive performance, yet these findings do not establish how to improve CoCrFeNiTi; moreover, some investigated alloys were brittle at 25 °C and displayed only limited plastic deformation at 600 °C. For equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but low hardness and load-bearing capability, what single intervention could improve hardness and mechanical performance while preserving those favorable characteristics and clarifying the relationship between microstructure and deformation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, a quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy, the processing and testing boundaries within which it should apply, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled microstructural and mechanical experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a small amount of silicon (Si) into the CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy will improve its hardness and mechanical performance while preserving its favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple crystal structure
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of silicon (Si) to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: The alloy is processed and tested under standard conditions, with a focus on evaluating its mechanical properties
generation.structural_mediator: The introduction of Si is expected to decrease the stability of the face-centered cubic (FCC) matrix, promoting transformation-induced plastic deformation and resulting in improved strength and work hardening ability
generation.mechanism: The addition of Si will lead to the formation of a metastable FCC matrix, which will undergo transformation to a hexagonal close-packed (HCP) phase during deformation, resulting in improved strength and work hardening ability
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy will exhibit improved hardness and mechanical performance, with a predicted increase in yield strength and ultimate tensile strength, while maintaining its favorable plasticity and machinability
generation.baseline: The unmodified CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple crystal structure
generation.boundary: The alloy composition, processing conditions, and testing parameters will be controlled to ensure that the introduction of Si is the only variable affecting the alloy's properties
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Si required to achieve the desired properties, as well as the potential effects of Si on the alloy's microstructure and phase composition, are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled experiment will be conducted to evaluate the effect of Si addition on the mechanical properties of the CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy. The alloy will be processed and tested under standard conditions, with a focus on evaluating its yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Si does not result in a significant improvement in the alloy's hardness and mechanical performance, as measured by the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

The Influence of Ti and Al on the Evolution of Microstructure and Mechanical Properties in Medium-Entropy and High-Entropy Alloys Based on AlxTixCrFe2Ni2

Abstract: This study focuses on the cobalt-free medium-to-high-entropy alloys AlxCrFe2Ni2 and AlxTixCrFe2Ni2, investigating the influence of Alx and Tix (where x = 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6) on the development of microstructural and mechanical properties in as-cast and annealed states. Structural changes were examined using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements, while mechanical properties were evaluated through Vickers hardness testing and compression testing. X-ray diffraction analysis of the AlxCrFe2Ni2 alloys confirmed that increasing the Al content in the as-cast state leads to the formation of a BCC phase, which completely dissolves into the FCC matrix after homogenization annealing. These single-phase alloys exhibit good ductility with relatively high strain hardening, such as the Al0.6CrFe2Ni2 alloy, which achieved a maximum compressive strength of σmax=1511 MPa at 50% deformation. A significant strengthening effect of Ti was observed in the AlxTixCrFe2Ni2 alloy

Extremely high strength and work hardening ability in a metastable high entropy alloy

Abstract: AbstractDesign of multi-phase high entropy alloys uses metastability of phases to tune the strain accommodation by favoring transformation and/or twinning during deformation. Inspired by this, here we present Si containing dual phase Fe42Mn28Co10Cr15Si5 high entropy alloy (DP-5Si-HEA) exhibiting very high strength (1.15 GPa) and work hardening (WH) ability. The addition of Si in DP-5Si-HEA decreased the stability of f.c.c. (γ) matrix thereby promoting pronounced transformation induced plastic deformation in both as-cast and grain refined DP-5Si-HEAs. Higher yet sustained WH ability in fine grained DP-5Si-HEA is associated with the uniform strain partitioning among the metastable γ phase and resultant h.c.p. (ε) phase thereby resulting in total elongation of 12%. Hence, design of dual phase HEAs for improved strength and work hardenability can be attained by tuning the metastability of γ matrix through proper choice of alloy chemistry from the abundant compositional space of HEAs.

Conclusions: Friction stir processing of Si containing HEA resulted in extremely refined metastable γ phase
